title: Prices and price tags
summary: What a card sells for is its own part of the shop: TCG Card Shop Simulator defines price tags as objects, a price-check screen, an atlas that holds tag artwork and a set of price-change kinds.
body: Prices are attached through price tag objects rather than being written onto the card itself, which is why labelling a card is its own step.
There is a dedicated screen for checking a price, so looking up what something is worth is a deliberate action in the shop.
The game counts several kinds of price change, so not every price adjustment is the same event.
What this entry does not tell you: actual prices, market movement or how much customers will pay. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Price tags are their own objects attached to goods.
Tag artwork comes from a shared atlas.
There is a screen dedicated to checking a price.
The game distinguishes several kinds of price change.
A price tag is an object a customer can interact with, built on a quad with its own material and a group for the interface.
facts.evidence: asset names: Interactable_PriceTag, PriceTagQuad, Mat_PriceTagInstanced, UI_PriceTag_Grp

facts.claim: Price tags are shipped per thing they can sit on: a card, an item box, a package box and a warehouse rack, each with its own group.
facts.evidence: asset names: UI_PriceTagCard_Grp, UI_PriceTagItemBox_Grp, UI_PriceTagPackageBox_Grp, UI_PriceTagWarehouseRack_Grp

facts.claim: The pricing side names a sell price field, a price button and an indicator for a price of zero.
facts.evidence: asset names: Sell Price, Price_Button, PriceZeroIndicator
